threads.title: Day 1 against day 2: much of each nutrient's spread is day-to-day noise, and the share differs by nutrient
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. Order: it runs after the implausible-day decision (diet-implausible-day-vs-person) and after the sequence and weekend terms are measured (diet-recall-nuisance-effects), because both inflate σ²w. It is read once repeat_kind is settled as replicates (detectors/repeats.recall_evidence; readings.repeat_kind_reading), or from wide day columns such as DR1TPROT beside DR2TPROT (usual_intake.day_columns, proposed). Per nutrient, a one-way random-effects decomposition into within-person σ²w (pooled Σuu) and between-person σ²b (nutrition.variance_components), on the scale the exposure enters the model (diet-error-grows-with-intake). The scale is printed with every number. Nutrients are ranked by 1 − λ, where λ = σ²b/(σ²b + σ²w/k_i) at each person's k_i recalls (Γ for the declared multivariate model). Measured on dietary_recalls.csv with all days kept: energy within/total 0.77–0.78 on the raw scale (λ for a 2-day mean 0.36–0.37), 0.76 and 0.39 on the log scale; protein 0.81 (λ 0.32), fat 0.82 (0.31), carbohydrate 0.84 (0.27), raw scale. All 20 implausible fixture days are day 1, 8 of them above 5,000 kcal, so the numbers are recomputed after that decision. Alternatives it must reject: a time course (repeats.trend: within-unit |ρ| ≥ 0.5 in ≥ 70% of units, or a period column; here the paired sign share rules it out: 53% of people fall from day 1 to day 2, sign p = 0.30); a sequence or weekend shift, removed first; reliability too low for any safe correction (diet-too-noisy-to-correct); too few repeaters for a stable λ (diet-few-replicate-persons).
threads.meaning: The recall days are replicates of one person's usual intake and are combined by the mean. The researcher confirms which outcome-model intakes are error-prone and declares measurement error (set_measurement_error: regression calibration) as a secondary analysis.

consumers.inference: The recalls are averaged. The coach explains that averaging k replicates cuts within-person variance k-fold, and that 600 recall rows are 300 people. People left with one day after the implausible-day decision carry k_i = 1.
consumers.prediction: The same aggregation, row-local per person. The number of days the deployed instrument must match is recorded (diet-deployment-measurement-heterogeneity).

consumers.inference: Every error-prone intake is calibrated jointly (multivariate RC: energy beside a nutrient, or all-components sources), on the exposure's model scale. The covariates are every other outcome-model column and never the outcome. Calibration runs inside each MI copy and is re-declared when the adjustment set changes. For residual or density models, energy is adjusted per recall day first.
consumers.prediction: Refused, with the reason: the deployed model sees recalls measured the same way. When deployment differs, see diet-deployment-measurement-heterogeneity.

consumers.inference: Distributions and shares below a cut-off come from the NCI method. For an association, regression calibration is the route. NCI predicted usual intakes (INDIVINT-style) count as regression calibration when their calibration model holds every outcome-model covariate, and they are the route for episodically consumed exposures (two-part RC, Kipnis 2009). DISTRIB draws, and BLUPs fitted without the outcome model's covariates, are refused for an association.
The calibrated estimate sits beside the uncorrected one as a declared secondary. Intervals come from a whole-chain bootstrap (PSUs within strata, or persons), which also carries λ's own uncertainty.
consumers.prediction: The reliability of the diet features is stated beside the honest score, because noise caps discrimination.

consumers.inference: The corrected coefficient sits beside the raw one, with λ as the reason. Observed-quintile contrasts are labeled wider than the usual-intake contrast.
consumers.prediction: Low importance of a low-λ nutrient is captioned as noise, not irrelevance.

consumers.inference: STROBE-nut nut-8.1 (days per person) and nut-12.3 (method, λ, its scale, and the assumption that recalls are unbiased), or the sentence 'intakes were not corrected for day-to-day variation'.
consumers.prediction: Attenuation is stated as a limitation, with the days per person.

threads.failure_prevented: A coefficient attenuated by half or more is reported as the association. With several error-prone intakes (energy beside a nutrient), one-at-a-time correction is also wrong, because the bias can go either way (Freedman 2011; Rosner 1990). Recall rows get analyzed as people, and one-day shares past a cut-off are wrong.
threads.magic: At exploration the canvas shows the day-1 against day-2 scatter and a Strip of each nutrient's within-person share: 'About three-quarters of the spread in one day's energy is day-to-day noise. A two-day mean carries about 39% of the true slope on the log scale your model uses.' [dietary_recalls.csv, all days kept; recomputed at run time after the implausible-day decision.] After the lock, the corrected effect sits beside the raw one with λ as the reason.
threads.layout: Card: Measurement error. Angles at exploration: the day-1 vs day-2 scatter, and between- vs within-person variance per nutrient as a Strip with its scale named (too-noisy nutrients are the Strip's bottom rows). After the lock, a Strip of raw vs corrected estimates per exposure.

Coefficients were corrected by multivariate regression calibration as a declared secondary analysis and are shown beside the uncorrected estimates, with intervals from a bootstrap of PSUs within strata that repeated the whole chain.

threads.title: A nutrient whose two recalls barely rank people, so no correction can rescue it
threads.detector: Uses the decomposition of diet-day-to-day-variance, on the same scale. It flags a nutrient whose person-mean reliability λ is below 0.1, or whose bootstrap lower bound (persons resampled) is below 0.1, or whose between-person variance is not positive. λ alone decides; correlation with energy is not part of the rule, because a nutrient with λ = 0.05 and r(energy) = 0.5 still gets a 20-fold correction. It must reject a nutrient with low spread but a reliable ranking (λ ≥ 0.3). Measured on dietary_recalls.csv: fiber_g day-1/day-2 r −0.11 (between-person variance not positive); sodium_mg r 0.01 (λ 0.02); protein_pct_kcal λ 0.07. The fixture is synthetic; real two-recall sodium is usually more reliable, so this fires rarely. Outcome-blind.
threads.meaning: Two recalls cannot rank people on this nutrient (here sodium and fiber).

threads.title: A share past a cut-off computed from one day is wrong, because one day's distribution is wider than usual intake
threads.detector: The usual_intake gate requires at least two people with two or more recalls (MIXTRAN; diet-few-replicate-persons covers the precision this gate does not check). The single-day distribution is set against the NCI usual-intake distribution (Box-Cox, nuisance terms), with the share past the cut-off under each. A one-day distribution is wider, so it overstates a share in the tail (an EAR below the median intake) and understates the share below an EAR that sits above the median (for example vitamin D or vitamin E in the US). Each component's share of zero recalls ranks amount-only against two-part (EPISODIC_SHARE 0.05, a stated convention). Outcome-blind.

threads.title: Many people report none: whether they form a non-consumer group depends on whether the zeros are people or days
threads.detector: Order: it runs after diet-zero-is-a-day. exposure_form.zero_share flags a share at exactly zero of 5% or more (MASS_AT_ZERO, rcspline's tied-extreme rule in rcs_knots), alongside the usual_intake zero-recall share. With replicates, the form ranking waits for the zero card's ruling: 'non-consumers as the reference plus a spline among consumers' ranks first only when the zeros are ruled structural; for episodic zeros, NCI two-part usual intake (or two-part RC) ranks first. Measured on dietary_recalls.csv: alcohol_pct_kcal is zero on 31.2% of days, but 29 people (9.7%) are zero on both days, against 9.5% expected under independence (35.7% × 26.7%), so the zeros look episodic; read on the person mean, MASS_AT_ZERO would fire and make those 29 a 'non-consumer' reference. Outcome-blind. It hands over to diet-former-consumers-in-reference when a lifetime-use column exists. Alternatives to reject: a missing code read as 0 (the what-a-zero-means reading) and a detection-limit zero.
threads.meaning: The zeros are true non-consumption, not missing values, and either structural (non-consumers) or episodic (days). The estimand covers the whole population or consumers only (nut-14).

consumers.inference: For structural zeros, non-consumers as the reference category plus a spline among consumers ranks first. For episodic zeros, the two-part usual intake ranks first. A consumers-only domain is an estimand change, asked at step 2.

threads.title: A zero is a day without the food, not necessarily a person who never eats it
threads.detector: For each food or nutrient with zeros and at least two replicate days: the zero share on day 1 (p1) and day 2 (p2), and the share zero on every day, compared with independence (p1 × p2) and with the arithmetic floor max(0, p1 + p2 − 1). Ranked by the share of zero days. The both-day zero share is an upper bound on never-consumers: people differ in how often they eat a food, which alone pushes both-day zeros above p1 × p2, so the independence test cannot tell never from rarely. Evidence that separates them is an FFQ 'never' column or a lifetime-use column (Tooze 2006 brings in an FFQ for this reason); otherwise the user is asked. Measured on dietary_recalls.csv: alcohol_pct_kcal zero on 35.7% of day-1 and 26.7% of day-2 recalls (31.2% of days), 9.7% of people zero on both, 9.5% expected under independence. With one day the two cannot be told apart, so the user is asked. Outcome-blind. Alternatives to reject: a not-done recall (every nutrient zero on the row; diet-recall-completeness), a missing code read as 0, and a detection-limit zero.

threads.title: The energy budget does not close: a source (usually alcohol) sits inside total energy but in no column
threads.detector: A row-level Atwater reconstruction (4P + 4C + 9F + 7A, fiber per the table's convention) against reported energy, read three ways. (a) At the model level, the share of energy the model's sources do not reconstruct (energy.omitted_energy) against MAX_OMITTED_SHARE of 5%. (b) At the row level, the ratio's distribution and its right-tail share, because a median-based check stays silent when only some rows carry the source. On a local NHANES extract the median ratio is 0.992, yet 10.1% of rows exceed 1.10, p99 is 1.45, and implied alcohol has p90 28.7 g. The sex split is printed with its estimator: implied alcohol = (E − 4P − 4C − 9F)/7 with negative gaps clipped at 0 gives a mean of 13.0 g in men vs 4.4 g in women. (c) Per-row residuals flag entry errors. Outcome-blind. Alternatives to reject: a unit error, which moves the median (kJ at 4.184), and fiber energy, which is small and has no heavy tail. Fiber-vs-carbohydrate conventions differ, so that is asked.

threads.title: Intake shifts by survey cycle, site, interviewer or food-composition release, and only some of those shifts are artifacts
threads.detector: For each batch-like column: survey cycle (SDDSRVYR, cycle_begin_year), site, wave, interviewer ID (NHANES DR1EXMER), interview mode, or a declared food-composition database release. It measures the share of each nutrient's variance the batch explains (η², or ICC for interviewers) after regressing out the batch's demographic make-up (age, sex), ranked by nutrient. A step change in one nutrient at a batch boundary, while energy, food-group intakes and other nutrients hold, points to a change in how the nutrient was computed or supplied. Values settle that a shift exists; its cause is asked and sorted into two kinds. Artifacts of measurement (a composition-table release, a protocol or mode change, interviewer drift) are removed or adjusted. Real changes in exposure (fortification, reformulation) are never batch-corrected. Outcome-blind. Alternatives it must reject: a secular trend (smooth across cycles and visible in food groups too) and case mix (removed by the demographic adjustment).

consumers.inference: Pooled cycles are flagged. Nutrients defined differently across releases (vitamin A IU→RAE, folate→DFE) are harmonized or not pooled (diet-nutrient-equivalents).
For artifacts, batch is a covariate in the outcome model (Nygaard 2016) or a stratifier, and interviewer is a random effect. Fortification and reformulation stay in the exposure.

threads.title: Only a handful of people have a second recall, so λ itself is too uncertain to correct with
threads.detector: The number of persons with two or more recalls, their share of the sample, and how they differ from single-recall persons (age, sex, day-1 intake; outcome-blind). The bootstrap interval of λ (or Γ) from resampling persons, ranked by interval width. The engine's gates are MIXTRAN's two repeaters (usual_intake MIN_REPEATERS = 2) and the calibration refusal when too few people have a recall; they say a number can be computed, not that it is stable. Replicate persons are rarely a random subsample: in NHANES since 2003 the second recall is attempted on all day-1 respondents, so completion is self-selected and the completer comparison is the evidence. Alternative: a large replicate subsample whose λ is precise.
threads.meaning: Whether the replicate subsample is large and representative enough for its λ to be used.

consumers.inference: λ's own uncertainty is propagated (the whole-chain bootstrap resamples it). Below a stated precision convention (for example a λ interval wider than ±50% of λ), RC is block-and-record, with the exit 'more replicates'.

The completer comparison is the MAR evidence (shared with diet-recall-completeness).

consumers.inference: Under the usual-intake question, day 1's deviation is correlated with the biomarker, so regression calibration's nondifferential assumption fails for day 1. Either the estimand is restated as acute, or a day-2-only replicate is the declared sensitivity analysis.
consumers.prediction: Deployment question: in use, will the recall be taken the day before the draw?

consumers.inference: Day-2-only analysis.
consumers.prediction: Score with day 2 only, the deployment-like input.

consumers.inference: 'Includes the acute effect of the previous day's intake'.
The timing and its handling are stated.

threads.failure_prevented: Consequential: HIGH for biomarker outcomes. Family K3, with a K4 timing face. Measurement error correlated with the outcome breaks regression calibration, and the association mixes yesterday's meal with habitual diet. A score rewards it, because yesterday's sodium predicts this morning's urine.
threads.magic: Day-1 recalls cover the 24 hours before the blood draw. For triglycerides, that is the meal you are measuring, not the diet. (Illustrative; needs a committed NHANES-derived fixture with a biomarker.)
threads.layout: Flow: the recall-day timeline against the exam, with the biomarker marked.
threads.sentence: Because the first recall covered the day before specimen collection, the analysis was repeated using the second recall only.
sources: NHANES MEC In-Person Dietary Interviewers Procedures Manual (day-1 recall at the MEC exam)
Carroll et al. 2006, Measurement Error in Nonlinear Models, 2nd ed.
threads.engine: new. usual_intake.py and the calibration stage exist.

threads.title: Sodium or potassium 'intake' is estimated from spot urine by an equation built on age, weight and creatinine
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. Extends the formula table of clin-derived-clinical-variables: a 24-h Na or K column reproduced from spot urine Na or K, creatinine, age, weight and height by the Kawasaki, Tanaka or INTERSALT equation. Names such as est_24h_na beside spot-urine columns also count. Units in mmol or mg are read.
threads.meaning: exposure_source: measured 24-h urine, estimated from spot urine (and by which equation), or self-report.

consumers.inference: The equation's inputs (age, weight, creatinine) are flagged: adjusting for them does not remove the association the equation builds in. Measured 24-h urine, or the spot Na/creatinine ratio, ranks first.
A J-curve in an estimated exposure is labeled as possibly induced by the equation.
A second equation and the raw ratio.
The equation is named.

threads.failure_prevented: Consequential: HIGH for sodium and potassium outcome analyses. Family K5, with K3. Equations built on age, weight and creatinine bake in associations with mortality and blood pressure, and they have been shown to change the sodium-mortality relationship.
threads.magic: est_na_24h is Kawasaki's equation of spot sodium, creatinine, age, weight and height (R2 1.00). Its J-curve may be the equation's, not the salt's. (Illustrative.)
threads.layout: Routing: the estimate drawn from its inputs.
threads.sentence: Sodium excretion estimated from spot urine (Kawasaki) was analyzed with a sensitivity analysis using the sodium-to-creatinine ratio.
sources: Kawasaki et al. 1993, Clin Exp Pharmacol Physiol 20:7
Cogswell et al. 2013, Am J Clin Nutr 98:1502
threads.engine: new.

threads.title: An FFQ is the only measure, so correcting for measurement error means borrowing a validation study from another population
threads.detector: Design fact. The exposure comes from an FFQ (diet-instrument-kind), and there is no internal replicate or reference (diet-ffq-recall-substudy is silent), so internal regression calibration is unavailable. Fires when the exposure is in the declared analysis.
threads.meaning: external_calibration: none, or a named validation study with its population, instrument version and calibration covariates, and whether it transports here.

consumers.inference: Regression calibration with the external lambda, as a labeled sensitivity analysis and never the primary. The bootstrap includes lambda's own uncertainty.
diet-invisible-exposure uses the external lambda to say what a null can rule out.
The source and the transport assumption are stated, or the limitation.

threads.failure_prevented: Consequential: MEDIUM. Family K3. Without this thread there are two failures. Either no correction is made and 'no association' is written silently, or a borrowed lambda from another population or instrument is applied as if exact, giving corrected intervals that are far too narrow.
threads.magic: There is no second measure of energy here. A null from this FFQ cannot rule out a true slope several times larger. (Illustrative.)
threads.layout: Angles: the observed estimate beside the corrected range under the borrowed lambda.
threads.sentence: A sensitivity analysis applied regression calibration using attenuation factors from an external validation study.
sources: Freedman et al. 2014, Am J Epidemiol 180:172
Carroll et al. 2006, Measurement Error in Nonlinear Models
threads.engine: partial: the calibration stage corrects from internal replicates or a substudy only. External lambda input is new.

top_moments: diet-day-to-day-variance (with diet-too-noisy-to-correct): 'About three-quarters of the spread in one day's energy is day-to-day noise. A two-day mean carries about 39% of the true slope on the log scale.' (dietary_recalls.csv). Before any model runs, the researcher learns that the headline coefficient will be attenuated by more than half, and declares regression calibration as the secondary analysis. In the same Strip, sodium and fiber sit at the bottom (day-1 vs day-2 r 0.01 and −0.11), so their nulls are labeled uninformative rather than corrected 50-fold.

diet-zero-is-a-day with diet-mass-at-zero and diet-former-consumers-in-reference: 'Alcohol is zero on 31% of recall days, but only 9.7% of people are zero on both, about what chance alone predicts (9.5%).' (dietary_recalls.csv). The 'non-drinker' reference a score-driven pipeline would build is people who happened not to drink on two days. Alcohol goes to the two-part model. When a lifetime-use column exists, never-drinkers are split from former drinkers, who often quit because they got sick.

diet-energy-carries-the-nutrient with diet-energy-related-outcome: 'fat_total moves with energy at r = 0.86. Unadjusted, the fat coefficient mostly measures how much people eat, and with BMI as the outcome, energy also lies on the path.' The researcher chooses between substitution at fixed energy and addition, and declares the with/without-energy pair. No score can make that choice.

diet-misreporting-tracks-body-size with diet-implausible-reporters: 'Below the one-day Goldberg cut-off: 38% of people with BMI ≥ 35, against 14% under 25. Reported energy does not rise with BMI (r = −0.03).' (local NHANES extract, Schofield weight-only BMR). The 'eat less, weigh more' pattern comes from the measurement, not from diet. A Goldberg exclusion would remove mostly obese participants and select on a BMI outcome, so it becomes a sensitivity analysis, and recall-based RC is labeled as not fixing this bias.

diet-energy-budget-gap: 'One day in ten has more energy than its protein, fat and carbohydrate can supply, and most of those days are men's. It is alcohol that was not exported as a column.' (local NHANES extract; the median check stays silent). Without it, a 'carbohydrate for fat at fixed energy' estimate silently moves alcohol too, and heavy drinkers are flagged as over-reporters.

diet-food-and-its-nutrients: 'Saturated fat is largely computed from your red-meat and dairy columns.' The app's own adjustment default (covariate_guesses.py Model 4) would adjust red meat for the nutrients it supplies, which removes part of its effect. The card moves those nutrients out of the confounder lane and into a declared secondary model.

diet-changed-because-of-disease: 'One in six follows a special or diabetic diet, and their sugar intake is much lower.' Their diet is a consequence of a diagnosis, so analyzed as a cause, sugar would look protective. The flag moves from the confounder lane to an eligibility sensitivity analysis, decided before any estimate. The flagged vs unflagged contrast reads predictors only, so it is allowed before the lock.

diet-instrument-kind: 'These are two FFQs a year apart, not two recall days.' Their agreement measures reproducibility, not validity. A correction built on it leaves most of the attenuation in place, and an FFQ cannot give a share below the EAR. This one answer decides whether RC, NCI and the EAR share are enabled or refused.

diet-healthy-lifestyle-cluster: 'Your top fiber quintile smokes half as often and is twice as likely to have a degree.' This Table 1 gradient reads predictors only, so it is shown before the lock. It leads the adjustment card and sets the E-value that accompanies the estimate, so a clean-looking association is read with the right distrust.

diet-deployment-measurement-heterogeneity (prediction): 'You trained on the mean of two recalls, and the clinic will take one.' Adding one-recall noise to the test folds pushes the calibration slope below 1. The score a pipeline would report is for an instrument the deployment will not use, so the app re-scores at deployment noise and offers recalibration.
journey_load:
Typical journey: pooled NHANES-style data, two 24-hour recalls, inference, a BMI or diabetes outcome, an alcohol column, and micronutrients.

As the catalog was written, this journey had about 13 to 15 asked questions and 6 to 8 surfaced noticings, roughly 20 interactions before the model. After the critic's tiers and the card consolidation, it has 5 new asked cards, each with one question, plus 4 surfaced noticings, about 9 interactions. About 12 stated lines go into the Flow and the methods, and 4 threads run silently.

**Asked (5 new cards)**
1. **Instrument and grain:** the instrument is confirmed as two 24-hour recalls, with the evidence pre-filled. Food rows, household rows and meal rows do not fire. The substudy, the biomarker and supplement contents are asked only when present. NHANES DR1T* totals are stated as food-only.
2. **Who is in (Flow):** one question: which screens are primary and which are sensitivity analyses. Day vs person is an option on the screen. Diet changed by disease and pregnancy are rows.
3. **Energy accounting and estimand:** substitution or addition, plus the declared with/without-energy pair for a BMI or diabetes outcome. The compositional reference is asked only for percent-energy columns. Alcohol's unit is asked only if it is recorded in drinks.
4. **Measurement error:** which intakes get regression calibration as the declared secondary. The card's Strip carries the too-noisy rows, λ intervals, the scale, season and the nuisance terms as stated lines.
5. **What a zero means: alcohol.** It covers episodic vs structural zeros, and the never/former split if ALQ is merged. At most two components per journey.

These existing cards absorb more questions at no new cost:
- **Adjustment card:** food-and-nutrients (only if foods are present) and season (only for a seasonal outcome).
- **Multiplicity card:** the nutrient-wide scan.
- **Units step:** the energy unit, which is silent here because the Atwater ratio is about 1.

**Surfaced (4)**
- The misreporting gradient, inside Who is in.
- The assessment-batch Strip for pooled cycles.
- The healthy-lifestyle gradient, on the adjustment card.
- The energy budget gap, only if no alcohol column closes it. In this journey it does not fire, so the fourth slot goes to too-noisy rows when they exist.

**Stated**
- The reliable-recall domain (DR1DRSTZ).
- The weight tier: WTDR2D, or the 4-year rule for 1999–2002.
- Nuisance terms, season coverage and the error scale.
- Nested fat parts and substitution support.
- EI:BMR refused as a covariate for a BMI outcome.
- DR1TNUMF routed out of the features.
- The meaningful increment.
- The invisible-exposure caption after the lock.

**Silent**
- Intake vs expenditure.
- The nutrient name test, including the alcohol identity.
- Median fill.
- Pattern guards.

**Prediction variant**
- The Measurement error question is replaced by the deployment-instrument question at intended use.
- The zero card offers frequency and amount features.
- The energy card states that the choice matters little to the score.
- The screen is applied in-fold only if deployment will screen too.
- About 4 asked and 3 surfaced.

**Rarer designs add one asked card at most:** an FFQ cohort (repeated-FFQ update rule, blanks), food-level files (sum to days), household surveys or CGM meal data. Each of these folds into the grain or intended-use question.
report:
I wrote the final dietary catalog: 55 threads, none cut. The critic recommended no cuts, so no thread was rejected by both the AutoML skeptic and the evidence checker.

**What changed**
- **Fixes:** all 18 were applied. The other 37 threads were rated sound and kept as written, apart from tier, rank and card placement.
- **Automate-silently threads:**
  - median-fill and patterns are now silent;
  - error-grows-with-intake and the dietary weight tier are now stated.
- **Tiers:** 27 asked, 8 surfaced, 16 stated and 4 silent. Most asked threads are conditional and fold into 5 consolidated cards or into questions that already exist, so a typical journey asks 5 new questions instead of 13 to 15. The `layout` and `rank_signal` fields name each thread's card.

**Rules I applied across the catalog**
1. **Magic numbers come from the data.** Each magic sentence is tagged with where its numbers come from: dietary_recalls.csv, a local NHANES extract, or illustrative and computed at run time. I replaced the numbers the fixture contradicted:
   - alcohol: 9.7% zero on both days, against 9.5% expected by chance;
   - the impossible 62%/9% zero pair;
   - the macronutrient sum to 100, which holds only with alcohol included;
   - 'everyone ate 7% less' on day 2: the drop is 0.8% on the log scale and only 53% of people fall;
   - the residualized r = 0.14, which is 0 by construction.
2. **Detectors run in a fixed order.** Order for the measurement-error chain:
   - the implausible day vs person decision comes first;
   - then the nuisance shift on the model's scale;
   - then the variance decomposition;
   - then the too-noisy and few-replicate flags;
   - then the regression calibration scale.

   Separately, zero-is-a-day runs before mass-at-zero ranks forms, and the delivered-residual test runs before intake_check rejects negative values.
3. **Several measured claims cannot be reproduced from the repo.** They come from `/Users/nhedglin/tabular-ml-lab/_tt_tmp_nhanes.csv`, which is gitignored, untracked and read-only. The committed `turbotab/sample_data/nhanes_dietary.csv` lacks body size and fat parts. These claims are marked in their sources. Committing a small derived fixture is Nolan's decision.

**Engine changes the fixes imply (the repo was read-only, so none were made)**
- `turbotab/core/usual_intake.py:459-466` (association_is_calibration) should refuse only DISTRIB draws and BLUPs fitted without the outcome model's covariates. Predicted intakes that include those covariates should count as regression calibration, which is the only route for episodic exposures.
- `turbotab/core/methods/calibration.py:332-336` refuses only a non-positive variance. It needs a λ floor and a bootstrap bound.
- `turbotab/core/recognizers.py:723` and `:834` reject any negative values before a delivered residual can be recognized.
- `turbotab/core/covariate_guesses.py:28-29` and `:91-92` adjust a food for the nutrients it supplies by default (Model 4).
- `turbotab/core/decisions.py:778` has no sum aggregation.
- Regression calibration runs on the column's raw scale only.
- `turbotab/nutrition.py:463` has no 4-year dietary weights.
- No code reads DR1DRSTZ, RIDEXMON or DRQSDIET.

**Purpose rules (for the separate verification)**
- diet-rare-events-sparse-categories needs an explicit clause: the outcome alone may set the parameter budget (categories, knots, parameters), as knots_by_rule and Riley's rule already do, but it may not choose the form.
- diet-ratio-features-share-the-outcome now refuses a feature as leakage only when it reads the same weight measurement as the outcome.

**Not verified**
- The critic's web checks were rate-limited, so Fraser 2009's conclusion and the size of Freedman 2014's attenuation factor were not checked online; the INDIVINT claim (Kipnis 2009) was checked from memory only.
- I did not run any Python. The fixture numbers are the critic's recomputations.
- The energy unit thread's '2,105 of 2,996 rows' count was not re-verified, so it is labeled for computation at run time.
